opportunities.description: Grants of up to $8,000 for women who already hold at least an associate's degree to pay for an accredited certificate or training program that leads to career advancement in a field where women are underrepresented.
opportunities.eligibility: Must identify as a woman; hold at least an associate's degree; be a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident. Program must start Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2027 (per the page) and be an accredited or licensed certificate or training program; degree programs, post-baccalaureate programs, and exam costs are not covered. Field must have under 50% women in the workforce, or for leadership training, under 50% women in senior roles (leadership applicants must be employed). Prior AAUW national award recipients are not eligible.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $8,000, paid in full at the start of the program.
opportunities.geo: United States, D.C., and listed U.S. territories
opportunities.notes: The official page lists a program start window of Jan 1 to Jun 30, 2027 for this Summer/Fall 2027 cycle, which looks inconsistent with the cycle name. Recheck when the window opens Jan 27, 2027. Field of Study reflects the page's examples (engineering, math, sciences, technology) and the leadership track; Business & Entrepreneurship stands in for executive leadership training.
opportunities.title: AAUW Career Development Grants, Summer/Fall 2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: Women with at least an associate's degree who are U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents.

opportunities.bestFit: Students from underserved communities interested in computer science, robotics, automation engineering and software development.
opportunities.description: Competitive scholarship for eligible U.S. high-school seniors to study software development or automation engineering. Offers up to $40,000 over four years, career mentorship and an opportunity for a paid internship.
opportunities.eligibility: High school senior in the U.S.; currently enrolled in or completed a high school or college dual-enrollment course in computer science, engineering, or robotics, or opts in to an Amazon-offered assessment; cumulative GPA of 2.3 or higher on a 4.0 scale; demonstrated financial need; authorized to work in the U.S.; plans to earn a bachelor's degree in an eligible field. Applicants choose one track: Automation Engineering or Software Development Engineering. Teacher recommendation due Jan 8, 2027. Finalists are notified in mid-January and complete an assessment by the end of January; winners are notified in mid-April 2027.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $10,000 annually for four years, depending on unmet financial need; mentorship and chance for paid Amazon internship (not guaranteed).
opportunities.nextStep: Share with high-school counselors, families, libraries and youth programs. Flag Jan 5 application deadline and Jan 8 teacher recommendation deadline. Consider cross-list in Village Notes and future Scholarships & Fellowships page.
opportunities.notes: 2026-11-05: Opportunity Type moved from the temporary 'Grant' to 'Scholarship' after Scholarship support was added to Airtable, the Community AI page, and the new Scholarships & Fellowships page. Publish To set to Community AI, Scholarships & Fellowships, and Village Notes (one record, cross-listed; no copies). Rechecked against the official page the same day: opens Nov 3, 2026; due Jan 5, 2027; teacher recommendation Jan 8, 2027; up to $10,000 a year for up to four years based on unmet need; Automation Engineering is new this cycle; the paid internship is a chance based on available positions, not a guarantee. Not the same program as the Amazon Future Engineer career tour. Next Expected Check Jan 9, 2027 to mark this cycle closed and watch for 2027-2028.
opportunities.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship 2026-2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: U.S. high school seniors planning related bachelor's degrees, with demonstrated financial need, GPA 2.3 or higher, and U.S. work authorization.

opportunities.description: Funding for U.S. graduate students to do language study and research abroad in regions important to U.S. national security, with a one-year federal service requirement afterward.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. citizen at the national deadline; enrolled in or applying to an accredited U.S. graduate degree program (master's, JD, or doctoral; certificate-only programs not eligible) and matriculated by the start date. Study must be in Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, or the Middle East. Programs start June 2027 to March 1, 2028. One-year federal service requirement. The official page shows Jan 20, 2027 for Fellowships in its banner, though one section label reads 'Scholarship'; confirm on the portal.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $25,000 for 25 to 52 weeks (preferred); up to $12,500 for 12 to 24 weeks.
opportunities.geo: U.S. students; study abroad in eligible regions
opportunities.title: Boren Fellowship 2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: U.S. citizen graduate students (master's, JD, or doctoral) at accredited U.S. institutions.

opportunities.description: Funding for U.S. undergraduates to study languages and cultures abroad in regions important to U.S. national security, with a one-year federal service requirement afterward.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. citizen at the national deadline; at least 18 with a high school diploma or GED; matriculated in an accredited U.S. associate's or bachelor's program and enrolled through the award. Study must be in Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America, or the Middle East (not Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand, and not a country of citizenship). Programs start June 2027 to March 1, 2028. One-year federal service requirement. Campus deadlines may be earlier.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $25,000 for 25 to 52 weeks (preferred); up to $12,500 for 12 to 24 weeks; up to $8,000 for 8 to 11 weeks (STEM majors only).
opportunities.geo: U.S. students; study abroad in eligible regions
opportunities.title: Boren Scholarship 2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: U.S. citizen undergraduates in an associate's or bachelor's program at an accredited U.S. institution.

opportunities.description: Last-dollar award that makes Connecticut community college tuition-free at any income level, after federal, state, and school aid.
opportunities.eligibility: Open to all income levels. Must have graduated high school or earned a GED; homeschooled students may apply. Covers costs left after other aid, with at least $250 a semester for eligible students. July 15 is the priority date; later applications are accepted, especially for spring starts.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Last-dollar coverage of tuition after other aid; eligible students receive at least $250 per semester.
opportunities.status: Rolling - priority date July 15; first-come, first-served
opportunities.title: Mary Ann Hadley Award (formerly PACT), Connecticut community college
opportunities.whoCanApply: High school graduates or GED holders (including homeschooled students) attending a Connecticut community college.

opportunities.description: Connecticut's state scholarship for high-achieving students with financial need who attend a four-year Connecticut public or nonprofit private college.
opportunities.eligibility: Top 20th percentile of the junior class (high school seniors) or senior class (college undergraduates), and/or a combined SAT of 1200+ or ACT of 25+. Student Aid Index at or below the yearly cutoff. Must attend a four-year Connecticut public or nonprofit private college. Apply by completing the FAFSA and having a high school counselor submit an application; the FAFSA must be in by Feb 15.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $5,250 a year at a four-year program; up to $4,650 a year at a two-year program.
opportunities.notes: The page states the FAFSA deadline as Feb 15; the 2027 date is applied for the 2027-2028 award year. Confirm the year and whether the counselor portal is open before marking Status Open.
opportunities.status: See official page - FAFSA and counselor application required
opportunities.title: Roberta B. Willis Scholarship, Need- and Merit-Based Award
opportunities.whoCanApply: Connecticut residents who are high school seniors (or college undergraduates) with strong grades or test scores and financial need.

opportunities.description: Need-based scholarships plus support services for students of Hispanic heritage at four-year colleges and graduate schools.
opportunities.eligibility: Identify as Hispanic (any race); U.S. citizen, permanent legal resident, or DACA recipient; minimum GPA 3.0 for high school and 2.5 for college and graduate applicants; plan to attend full time at an accredited public or nonprofit four-year university or graduate school in the U.S.; complete the FAFSA. 2026 cycle: profile opened Jan 5, deadline Feb 15, 2026.
opportunities.fundingDetails: $500 to $5,000 based on relative need, depending on available funds.
opportunities.notes: 2026 cycle closed. Recheck early January 2027 for the 2027 application; create a new cycle record only if dates or terms change, otherwise update this one with the new dates.
opportunities.title: HSF Scholar Program 2026
opportunities.whoCanApply: Students who identify as Hispanic: high school seniors, college students, and graduate students.

opportunities.description: Last-dollar scholarship for high-achieving high school seniors with financial need, applied after a college's own aid, for a four-year bachelor's degree at any accredited college.
opportunities.eligibility: Minimum unweighted GPA of 3.75; at least one SAT, ACT, AP, or IB score (no minimum); family gross income up to $95,000; must live in the U.S. or a U.S. territory and attend all four years of high school there (U.S. citizenship not required). Gap-year, GED, and currently enrolled college students are not eligible. Renewal is annual at the Foundation's discretion.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $55,000 a year for up to four years, depending on cost of attendance and other aid. Covers tuition, room and board, books, and required fees. Online programs are not covered.
opportunities.notes: Seeded 2026-11-05 for the Scholarships & Fellowships page. Deadline is Nov 11, 2026; recheck Nov 12 to mark this cycle closed and watch for the 2028 cycle.
opportunities.title: Cooke College Scholarship Program 2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: High school seniors graduating in spring 2027 who will enroll full time at an accredited four-year college in fall 2027.

opportunities.description: Unrestricted grants paid directly to women 35 and older with financial need who are working toward technical or vocational training, a first associate's degree, or a first bachelor's degree.
opportunities.eligibility: Must be 35 or older, self-identify and present as a woman, show financial need, and pursue technical or vocational education, a first associate's degree, or a first bachelor's degree at an accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. Applications and recommendation letters due Feb 12, 2027; applicants notified Jul 31, 2027.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $3,000 a year, paid to the recipient for non-tuition costs, renewable for up to five years.
opportunities.geo: Nationwide; institution must be in the U.S.
opportunities.title: Jeannette Rankin National Scholar Grant 2026-2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: Women age 35 or older with financial need.

opportunities.description: A $20,000 flexible scholarship plus a laptop, book credits, emergency funds, and support through college, for Texas high school seniors heading to Texas public universities.
opportunities.eligibility: Must be a high school senior graduating from a Texas high school; take part in an approved college readiness program in grades 11 and 12; be Pell Grant eligible; have at least a 2.4 GPA; and plan to attend an accredited four-year public college or university in Texas. Finalists announced Jan 21, 2027; finalist materials due Mar 31, 2027; scholars announced May 20, 2027.
opportunities.fundingDetails: $20,000 flexible scholarship usable for tuition, fees, full cost of attendance, graduate school, loan repayment, study abroad, and internship stipends; also a laptop, book credits, and emergency funds. About 500 scholars a year.
opportunities.geo: Texas high school graduates attending Texas public four-year institutions
opportunities.title: Dell Scholars Program 2027
opportunities.whoCanApply: Texas high school seniors in an approved college readiness program in grades 11 and 12.

opportunities.description: Up to $5,000 for Pell Grant recipients to study or intern abroad for credit, including summer and fall 2027 programs.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. citizen undergraduate with high financial need who receives a Federal Pell Grant at application, or will during the program. Covers credit-bearing study or career-oriented internships abroad. Programs must start May 1, 2027 to Apr 30, 2028. Student deadline Feb 25, 2027 (11:59pm PT); advisor certification Mar 4, 2027. A separate Skills for America award serves two-year college students.
opportunities.fundingDetails: Up to $5,000; limited supplemental funding for STEM and critical language study. Covers tuition, room and board, books, travel, insurance, and passport and visa fees.
opportunities.geo: U.S. citizens at U.S. institutions; study or intern abroad
opportunities.notes: Open date is stated only as mid-January 2027, so Application Opens is blank. Set it and change Status to Open when the portal opens.
opportunities.title: Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship, Spring 2027 application
opportunities.whoCanApply: U.S. citizen undergraduates receiving a Federal Pell Grant, from any type of institution.

opportunities.description: Three years of support for early-career graduate students in research-based STEM and social science degree programs: a yearly stipend plus a cost-of-education allowance paid to the school.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident. Final-year bachelor's students, bachelor's holders with no graduate enrollment, joint bachelor's-master's students in the final undergraduate or first graduate year, or first-year students in a first graduate degree. Not eligible: anyone with a master's, doctoral, or terminal degree, more than one year of graduate study, or a prior fellowship acceptance. Must plan a research-based graduate degree in an eligible field listed in the NOFO; MD, JD, MBA, DVM and joint professional degrees are excluded. 2026 field deadlines were Oct 19 to 23, 2026.
opportunities.fundingDetails: $37,000 a year stipend plus a $16,000 a year cost-of-education allowance to the institution; a five-year award with three years of support.
opportunities.notes: Listed as a closed, recurring fellowship so visitors can plan for the next competition. Do not carry these dates forward; recheck the new NOFO.
opportunities.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP), 2026 competition
opportunities.whoCanApply: U.S. citizens, nationals, or permanent residents who are college seniors, bachelor's holders not yet in graduate school, or first-year graduate students.
